covers: rmodels.c's LoadModel on OBJ files, as 6.2's LoadOBJ and ProcessMaterialsOBJ make them from tinyobj_loader_c's reading (makeobj.py's files, and raylib's own cube.obj): polygons split into fans, a mesh at each g and o line with faces after it (lines with none between, a name given again, o lines, lines at the end) and at each change of material, faces before any usemtl joining the next material's mesh, a usemtl naming no material of the library given material 0 and the material after it joined to its mesh, a group's start counted in f lines against triangles (a polygon, and faces of 1 and 2 corners, before it moving the mesh's start), each mesh's material its last face's; the vertices unindexed, texture coordinates' v turned, a corner without a normal (0, 1, 0) and one without texture coordinates (0, 0), corners naming positions, texture coordinates and normals the file doesn't have ((0, 0, 0), (0, 0) and (0, 1, 0)) and ones on lines after the face, negative numbers, a position's w and six-value positions' colors not read, colors white; the materials the library's in its order, a name given twice the last's, the diffuse texture or else Kd, Ks and the specular texture, the bump texture (the last bump or map_bump line's; map_Bump not read) as the normal map with Ns as its value, Ke, the displacement texture as the height map, a missing texture none, materials giving no Kd, Ks, Ke or Ns (tinyobj_loader_c's black and 1); a missing library and none giving the default material alone; an empty file and a missing one read as files raylib can't read; a Latin-1 file and library, a material named with é matched by name
notes: 6.2's LoadOBJ is the oracle: 5.5's reads a corner without a normal or texture coordinates, or naming one the file doesn't have, at tinyobj's index, out of its arrays (built against 5.5, this reference crashes on shapes.obj and plain.obj), which 6.2 fixed. Where raylib's LoadModel can't read a file it gives a model without meshes, printed as failed, and LoadModelAsync fails. The textures are RGBA PNGs: helix-raylib's file textures say PIXELFORMAT_UNCOMPRESSED_R8G8B8A8 whatever the file's channels. cube.obj is raylib's (CC0, by Ramon Santamaria), taken from the oracle's own source. Numbers differ by a float's rounding: helix-formats reads them as doubles, rounded to floats, where tinyobj_loader_c sums their digits in doubles.
